processing: Young mountain buds are made into a straight, needle-shaped green tea, using a mix of traditional craft and modern technology.
harvest_season: Early spring; the tender buds are picked around March.
appearance_dry: Tight, slender, straight needles, moist green and visibly downy.
appearance_wet: Tender, even, bright green buds that open like small flowers.
taste_profile: High, clean fragrance with a fresh, mellow and brisk taste.

brewing.notes: Typical handling for a tender needle green: a glass shows the buds well, and water near boiling will flatten it. Add a little more time on each steep.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year early spring tea, like other fine Chongqing greens, and meant to be drunk within about a year. Look for the harvest date on the pack. The earliest March buds are the point of the tea, so old stock has little to recommend it.
description:
Taibai Yinzhen is a needle-shaped green tea from Wanzhou in Chongqing, in the Three Gorges stretch of the Yangtze. The name means 'Taibai silver needle', and it is sold as a premium green.

It is made from young high-mountain buds picked in early spring, and the finish is straight, slim and downy. Tea this tender gives a pale, clean cup, so its appeal lies in freshness and not in strength.

The producer describes a high, pure fragrance and a fresh, mellow, brisk taste, which fits its class. Keep the water off the boil and do not overload the glass, because cooked bud tastes flat and vegetal.

In practice this is closely tied to one company's brand, sold under the Wanxian label, so the name on a pack generally tells you who made it. Ask for the harvest date, as you would with any spring green.
history:
The tea is documented mainly through its producer in Wanzhou, which presents it as its flagship and claims more than ten prizes in national and Chongqing tea competitions, including the Zhonglü Cup and Sanxia Cup. These are the company's own account.

In 2008 and 2010 it was nominated in the Chongqing top ten famous teas, and in 2010 it was named a Chongqing famous-brand farm product. A first Taibai Yinzhen tea culture festival took place in Wanzhou in April 2011, where it took a gold award in the tea competition held at the event.
